answer:
HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded natural-language answer)

In the PCA conducted on the forms of capital sampled in hundred-year time slices (capital.csv: 39 century-slices, 4300→500 BCE, 12 Z-standardized proxy variables), the symbolic-capital components — house size (Zhausgr), daggers (ZDolch), and hatchets/swords (ZAxtSchwert) — are characterized as follows.

On the first principal component (PC1, 31.1% of variance), all three carry moderately POSITIVE loadings — hatchets/swords ≈ +0.30, daggers ≈ +0.27, house size ≈ +0.22. PC1 itself is the dominant temporal axis of capital: its century scores run from strongly negative values in the Early Neolithic (−2.0 to −1.8 at 4300–3600 BCE) to strongly positive values around the Middle Bronze Age (+4.5 at ~1100 BCE) and back down (~+0.8 by 500 BCE). Hence the symbolic-capital forms co-vary positively with this main, time-bound amplification of capital rather than opposing it.

In their distribution across the second principal component (PC2, 20.0% of variance), the three are NOT uniform. House size spreads widely along PC2 (loading ≈ +0.33; correlation with the PC2 scores ≈ 0.50), i.e., it contributes strongly to the secondary axis that differentiates phases within the sequence (high-PC2 episode ~3500–1300 BCE, peaking near 3200 and 1300 BCE, versus the low-PC2 Early-Neolithic and terminal ~1000–500 BCE phases). In contrast, daggers and hatchets/swords sit essentially on the PC1 axis: their PC2 loadings are near zero (≈ +0.07 and ≈ +0.05) and their correlations with PC2 scores are weak (≈ 0.11 and 0.08), so their variation is almost entirely captured by PC1 and they do not differentiate along the second component.

Consolidated reading: symbolic prestige forms (dagger, hatchet/sword) are moderate, positive constituents of the main capital axis while remaining narrowly clustered around PC1 (little PC2 spread); house size likewise loads positively on PC1 (~0.22) but additionally spreads markedly across PC2 (~0.33), making it the symbolic-capital component that carries a distinct secondary dimension of variation. This qualitative pattern is robust to excluding the atypical ZSichel variable (PC2 loadings without ZSichel: house size ≈ 0.37 vs. dagger ≈ 0.13, hatchet/sword ≈ 0.07).

payload.workflow: 1) Parsed capital.csv with comma decimals (39 century slices, BCE 4300-500); dropped BCE/group/color; kept 12 pre-standardized capital Z-variables. 2) PCA via SVD on the standardized 39x12 matrix (correlation-based; re-standardization a near no-op). 3) Extracted PC1/PC2 loadings for symbolic proxies (Zhausgr, ZDolch, ZAxtSchwert) and century PC scores. 4) Quantified 'spread across PC2' as PC2 loading (primary) plus correlation with PC2 scores and PC2-score range/std. 5) Robustness check excluding ZSichel. 6) Wrote analysis.py (executed) and saved loadings/scores/summary CSV outputs.
payload.hypothesis: In the PCA on forms of capital in hundred-year time slices, symbolic-capital components (house size, daggers, hatchets/swords) all show moderately positive PC1 loadings (≈0.22-0.30), aligning them with the main temporal axis of capital accumulation; their PC2 distribution differs — house size spreads widely along PC2 (loading ≈0.33, r≈0.5) while daggers and hatchets/swords sit near the PC2 axis (loadings ≈0.05-0.07, r≈0.08-0.11), indicating prestige weapons track the dominant axis without secondary differentiation, whereas house size carries a distinct secondary dimension of variation.
